_comment: Copy to backend/mcp.json and edit the paths. mcp.json is gitignored. ${KEEPER_ROOT} expands to the app root, so one config works on the host AND in the container. The manager applies a read-only filter by default; 'tools' is an explicit allowlist (only these pass), 'deny' blocks by name, and 'required' names the tools this server MUST provide - if one is missing the server shows as degraded in /state and on the dashboard instead of quietly going absent. uvx servers pin 'mcp<2' because the published fetch/time/git servers target the mcp 1.x API while the client uses mcp 2.x. 'propose' names tools that CHANGE something: they skip the read-only filter but never run when the model calls them; calling one records a proposal, the person sees the exact arguments and approves or declines, and only an approved one runs (see proposals.py). 'deny' still wins over 'propose'. 'requires_env' keeps a server off, and reported as off rather than broken, until those variables are set in backend/.env.

servers.name: google
servers._note: Gmail + Calendar via taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp. Least privilege: gmail:send (read, labels, drafts, send) and calendar:full, nothing else. Reads are an explicit allowlist, because a name filter lags each new server's verbs. Sending and changing events sit under 'propose': the model can only ask, you approve the exact payload. 'fixed_args' sets the account from backend/.env; the model never sees or chooses it. First run: scripts/google_auth.py.

_watch_comment: Tools the proactive loop polls for what is NEW, scored against memory like any feed item. Only tools whose entries carry their own identity belong here (a commit log, a listing, a calendar); a web search returns the same results every time and would have the Keeper announce old news as a discovery. See sources.py.
